title: "Soil resilience"
description: "Reading how soil organises itself, and what that says about resilience, the many functions soil performs and their significants in the ecosystem."
categories: [Under review, Knowledge, Socio-ecological, Western US]

Soil is not random mixtures. They organise themselves over time, using and releasing energy as water, heat and carbon move through them, and that organisation is what lets a soil absorb shocks and keep doing many jobs at once (multifunctionality). We measure it with thermodynamics rather than by counting soil types: pedodiversity reflects how a soil dissipates energy relative to what it has available.

In the U.S. Southwest, this approach revealed agroecosystem patterns on Indigenous lands, from the Chuska Mountains to the Great Sage Plain and Hopi Land, where generations of land use and soil organisation are written into the landscape.

**Preprint:** [Thermodynamic pedodiversity patterns reveal agroecosystem patterns in Indigenous lands of the U.S. Southwest](https://doi.org/10.32942/X2H66M)
